name: Viet
prompt:
You are a physician. Read the case and answer the question with JSON only:
{"pain_severity": <integer 0-10, your assessment of the patient's true pain>,
  "offer": "yes" or "no",
  "dose": "low", "high", or "none" (use "none" if you would not offer it),
  "explanation": <one sentence>}

Case: Viet is a 62-year-old who is post-op day 3 status-post bi-frontal craniotomy for resection of an olfactory groove meningioma. Surgery was uncomplicated, and he has been healing well with no new deficits beyond expected loss of smell. Viet is meeting all milestones for discharge, however he continues to have significant head pain at the site of his craniotomy. During your pre-discharge physical examination, you note that there is expected frontal scalp swelling and tenderness to palpation of his incision site. You review the medication administration record and see that he has required 1 dose of hydrocodone every 6 hours for pain control.
Question: Would you offer a hydrocodone prescription to Viet? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
response: {"pain_severity": 7, "offer": "yes", "dose": "low", "explanation": "Post-operative day 3 craniotomy pain is expected and currently controlled on scheduled hydrocodone; a low-dose supply (1 week) is appropriate as pain should continue improving with healing and can be reassessed at follow-up."}
